newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close flat in quiet trading.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close flat in quiet trading.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed little changed in listless trade on Tuesday, with the market awaiting U.S. economic data out on Wednesday to provide direction, analysts said.

"There's not much to talk about today. It's been really slow and there's no data to focus on," said Harvinder Kalirai, a Canadian analyst with financial analysis firm I.D.E.A. "The U.S. auction was the main focus of the day and it seems to have gone all right."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond ended the session unchanged at C$116.60 to yield 6.706 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 5/32 to yield 6.69 percent. The spread between the bonds widened to two basis points from nil at Monday's close.

"Everything is basically unchanged or within a nickel or a dime. I think generally there's buying though. When the market came off earlier in the day, accounts came in to buy in small amounts," said Barry Allan, vice president of global fixed income with Altamira Investment Services Inc.
Allan said some of the buying -- which was providing support for the market -- was prompted by portfolio managers looking to put cash to work before quarter's end.
